headline: Discussed draft land use goals for the Winooski Comprehensive Plan, including the Gilbrook area.
summary: Members reviewed draft text of the land use section of the Winooski Comprehensive Plan. Topics included the future land use map, wetlands in Gilbrook, building heights, and neighborhood hubs. Members approved the previous meeting minutes 4-0, with one abstention.
decisions: Approved the September 10, 2026 meeting minutes 4-0, with John abstaining.

plain_text:
9/24/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Mike O’Brien, Chair; John Baker, Vice Chair; Matt Gile; Brian Colombini; 
Ruby Tetrick; James Paradissis; Trevor Thomas
City Staff Present:
Guests Present: Thomas Renner, Mayor; Sam Mathisson; Amelia Kennedy; Wyatt Knowlton; 
Adi Shore; Owen Fellows; Theo Murphy; Bre Hetzer
Call to Order by: Mike
Meeting Start Time: 6:32 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by Brian, seconded by Matt, to approve the September 10, 2026 meeting minutes. Voting: 
4-0 (John abstained). Motion carried.
Discussion: Winooski Comprehensive Plan – The draft Land Use goals and actions 
Ravi said that this item is a continuation from the previous meeting’s discussion on the future 
land use map and that the focus will be on the draft text of the land use section of the 
Comprehensive Plan. Ravi said that he will be talking to Burlington and Colchester to check 
alignment of the future land use map with neighboring municipalities. Mike suggested reaching 
out to South Burlington.
Mike asked about the demographics. Ravi said that he pulled the demographics data from the 
compilation the consultants put together for the Equitable Housing Needs Assessment. Ravi 
said that the consultants, UVM Center for Rural Studies, averaged years of US Census 
American Community Survey data to get a better generalized estimate of demographic data. 
Mike asked about the utilization of 2010 and 2020 Census data. Ravi said he thinks that the 2010 
and 2020 Census data may be incorporated in this compilation.
Ravi said that UVM Center for Rural Studies will be presenting the Equitable Housing Needs 
Assessment to the Housing Commission and City Council. Mike suggested that they present to 
the Planning Commission for the explanation of the data methodology and the project 
recommendations. Mike also suggested including the 2020 and 2010 US Census data in the text 
as well to show growth, and using more current data.
Ravi reviewed the projected population growth that consultants compiled for the the Chittenden 
County Regional Planning Commission regional plan. Ravi said that he can distribute 
background on the methods for this population projection after the meeting.
Mike and Ravi reviewed the household size data. Mike noted that the data appears to align with 
the overall national trend of shrinking household sizes.
John asked if this draft is how the final product will look. Ravi said no and that he will work with 
Communications Director Paul Sarne to package the plan later this year.
Ravi reviewed the edits to the future land use map the commission suggested during the last 
meeting. Trevor asked about discussing Gilbrook further, considering the amount of wetlands in 
Gilbrook. Trevor asked about the ownership of lands in Gilbrook and whether the Town of 
Colchester owns lands in Gilbrook. Mike said that 20 years ago, the City had been interested in 
maintaining the flexibility of that portion of Gilbrook in case of an opportunity for development. 
Ravi showed the commission the location of possible wetlands in the northern portion of 
Gilbrook. Mike suggested continued conversations about Gilbrook, and reviewing feedback. 
Trevor suggested reviewing the Parks and Open Space Master Plan recommendations for 
Gilbrook. John recommended maintaining the flexibility of having the northern section of Gilbrook 
viable for conservation and potential future development. Ravi said that if flexibility is the intent, 
keeping the map as-is would be the best path forward, because if the City identifies the area as 
conservation in the future land use map, the City wouldn’t be able to allow for development 
because this is incompatible with the future land use map.
Brian suggested changing the word “divide” in the description of the future land use map to 
“identify” or a similar term that is less harsh.
Ravi gave an overview of the draft text, and asked if the commission has suggestions for 
defining “transition/infill”. Mike suggested keeping the description open ended.
Ravi and the commission reviewed the draft goals and objectives. Mike asked about building 
height limitations in the Gateway District. Ravi said that the height limit is 4.5 to 5.5 stories. 
Thomas asked about Federal Aviation Administration limitations. Ravi said that there aren’t any 
such limitations. Mike and Ravi reviewed the height limitations for the downtown core. John 
talked about the potential for neighborhood commercial uses outside of the downtown area. Ravi 
reviewed the zoning allowances for neighborhood commercial uses, and suggested identifying 
potential neighborhood hubs. Ravi and the commission discussed the need to not restrict the 
uses on properties to particular locations but to encourage particular intersections into 
neighborhood hubs.
Brian mentioned that neighboring municipalities have had discussions about increasing building 
height along corridors, such as Essex Junction. John discussed the incompatibility of tall 
buildings directly adjacent to smaller-scale buildings, and suggested a transitional zone between 
the corridors and lower intensity residential areas.
Mike asked if the Local Resources Advisory Board has reviewed the draft goals and objectives. 
Ravi said they have and that he can share this with them during their next meeting.
The commission discussed the draft objective on walkability. John asked about the status of 
Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB) in the circle. Thomas said that more will be 
installed as part of the bridge project. Brian asked if City Council has thought about the 
possibility of using the circle for different types of events considering the traffic pattern shift with 
the bridge construction, and asked if such a goal could be identified in the Comprehensive Plan.
Mike asked the audience if they had any questions. Sam Mathisson asked for more information 
about the Local Resources Advisory Board. Ravi reviewed the Local Resources Advisory 
Board’s role and responsibilities. Wyatt Knowlton asked about maintenance requirements for 
buildings. Ravi pointed out the minimum housing complaint form one can fill out for possible 
safety issues.
Brian asked for clarification on adaptive reuse. Ravi said that the Local Resources Advisory 
Board has been more focus on maintaining the integrity and feel of buildings with the 
improvement and reuse of historic buildings. Brian suggested adding a term similar to “adaptive 
reuse” to the objective on infill development, such as “thoughtfully adapts to the existing 
neighborhood” to indicate the desire for compatibility.
City Updates
Updates from the Mayor
Thomas reviewed recent City Council discussions, including the longevity bonus 
pay policy, the Burlington Airport noise mitigation program, and permission to the 
fire department for fundraising.
Updates from the Inclusion and Belonging Commission
Updates from City Staff
Ravi said that the ribbon cutting for Main Street will be on Wednesday, September 
30th from 10 am to 12 pm, that the Development Review Board continued the public 
hearing for the Armory to October 15th.
Other Business
Adjourn
Motion by: John
Second: Matt
Meeting End Time: 7:52 pm
